newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Budget factored into Australia GDP outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Budget factored into Australia GDP outlook.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said on Monday that its GDP forecasts had allowed for the dampening effect of the August budget cuts.

"In the budget forecasts themselves, the forecasts incorporate a small reduction in the growth outlook as a result of the fiscal consolidation," Treasury deputy secretary Gary Potts told a parliamentary committee.
The Australian government, in its August 20 budget, forecast growth to slow to 3.5 percent in the 1996/97 year, compared with 4.1 percent in the previous year.
For later years Treasury also issues projections which have a lower status than the forecasts for the current year.
These projections are used as forecasting assumptions for the fiscal forward estimates.

Asked why the 1997/98 projection showed 3.25 percent growth compared with 3.5 percent in later years, Potts said: "Well we thought it was appropriate to allow for the effects of fiscal consolidation, but to go no further than that in attempting to
produce forecasts which would allow for cyclical effects.
"So we were simply allowing for the impact of the fiscal consolidation in very broad terms," he said.
"In 1997/98, we would expect there would be some reduction in demand as a result of the fiscal consolidation package," he said.
